# `error-collapsed-to-absence`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a catch that converts every error to `null` or another empty optional
result.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Callers can no longer distinguish a valid absence from an operation that failed.

## When it fires

Enable it where failure and not-found are separate domain outcomes; deliberate
lossy probing can be suppressed locally. A fallback tested on the spot is the
point rather than a lost failure: `(x catch null) == null`,
`if (x catch null) |value|`, and `catch false` as an operand of `!`, `and` or
`or` in an `if` or `while` condition are not reported. Neither is a call whose
every failure means the input has no result: one that can fail in only one way
(checked `std.math` arithmetic, an allocation, `bufPrint`, a `*std.Io.Writer`
method, or a function the file declares with a one-error set, as
`lost-error-context` knows them), `std.math` division, and a `parse` function
(`parseInt`, `parse_int`, ...) given no allocator or reader.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn cachedSize(path: []const u8) ?u32 {
    return readSize(path) catch null;
}

fn readSize(path: []const u8) !u32 {
    return @intCast(path.len);
}
```
